_comment: Session library + week templates. A session's 'zone' names a row of the zones table (E, LT1, MP, RP, ST, T, VO2, VO2s, S). Key sessions progress through 'steps' (one per build week of the block); 'recover' is the recovery-week variant (null = drop it that week). 'q' = minutes of quality work at the zone; the rest of the session counts as easy.

swim-aerobic.name: Aerobic swim
swim-aerobic.set: 300 easy · 4×50 drill · 8×100 @ CSS +6–8″ (15″ rest) · 200 pull easy
swim-aerobic.why: Aerobic volume with technique. Short rests keep it continuous without going hard.

swim-endurance.name: Endurance swim
swim-endurance.why: Longer reps at the same easy pace. Per Deckard, 5×500 at Z2 is a touch slower than 20×100 at Z2, and that's correct.

swim-vo2.name: Swim VO2
swim-vo2.why: The swim's ceiling session: reps at 400 m race pace.

swim-css.name: CSS swim
swim-css.why: Half-distance race specificity: long, steady, at threshold pace.

swim-ow.name: Open water
swim-ow.set: Continuous 1.5–2 km in open water, sighting every 6–8 strokes, 4×1′ race effort
swim-ow.why: Sighting, wetsuit, and pacing without walls.

swim-test-400.name: Swim test: 400 + 200 TT
swim-test-400.set: 400 easy · 4×50 build · 400 TT all-out · 300 easy · 200 TT all-out · 200 easy
swim-test-400.why: Deckard profiles the swim with a ~500 yd time trial. 400 + 200 also gives CSS = 200 / (T400 − T200) per metre.

bike-easy.name: Easy spin
bike-easy.set: Easy, high cadence, well below LT1
bike-easy.why: Volume that costs nothing to recover from.

bike-lt1.name: LT1 ride
bike-lt1.set: 15′ easy · steady just under LT1 · 10′ easy. Keep HR flat; if it drifts more than 5%, back off.
bike-lt1.why: Per Deckard, long easy work under LT1 is the primary VO2max driver: stroke volume, mitochondria, fat oxidation. The top of easy, never above it.

bike-long.name: Long ride
bike-long.set: Below LT1 the whole way · fuel 60–90 g carbs/h from the start
bike-long.why: Big aerobic stimulus, durability, gut training.

bike-vo2-3015.name: VO2 30/15s

steps.set: 15′ warm-up · 3 × (10 × 30″ on / 15″ off) · 3′ easy between sets · cool-down

bike-vo2-3015.how: The 15″ off is pedalled at ~50% of 5′ power. Never coast: coasting turns it glycolytic (Deckard). If you're fading, drop the 30″ target by 10–20 W and keep the 15″ strict.
bike-vo2-3015.why: Rønnestad's 30/15 protocol keeps you near VO2max for longer than steady 4′ reps. It's the main ceiling session.

bike-vo2-4min.name: VO2 4′ reps
bike-vo2-4min.how: Deckard anchors these at ~92% of 4′ power, which is why they feel hard. First rep should feel controlled.
bike-vo2-4min.why: The second ceiling session in a VO2 block. Long reps load stroke volume.

bike-torque.name: Torque / low cadence
bike-torque.how: Deckard uses torque work to train threshold without sitting right on threshold. Seated, quiet upper body.
bike-torque.why: Raises LT2 and nudges VLamax down while VO2max carries over.

bike-threshold.name: Threshold
bike-threshold.how: Per Deckard, within 10% under threshold is fine; 5% over is a different session that costs days.
bike-threshold.why: Extends time at LT2: the utilization side of the profile.

bike-race-pace.name: 70.3 race-pace ride

steps.set: 30′ easy · 2 × 30′ @ 70.3 power (10′ easy) · easy to finish

bike-race-pace.how: Race nutrition exactly as planned for race day. Aero position for every race-pace minute.

bike-test-5.name: Bike test: 5′ all-out
bike-test-5.set: 20′ progressive warm-up incl. 3 × 1′ hard · 10′ easy · 5′ ALL-OUT, evenly paced · 20′ easy
bike-test-5.why: Deckard's anchor: 5′ power ≈ power at VO2max. LT1 and LT2 are read as % of it (standard ≈ 50 / 75 / 100%).

bike-test-20.name: Bike test: 20′ TT
bike-test-20.set: 20′ warm-up incl. 2 × 3′ firm · 5′ easy · 20′ TT, start conservative · 20′ easy
bike-test-20.why: LT2 ≈ 90% of 20′ power (Deckard's safe estimate). A lab lactate step test is better if you can book one; it also gives LT1.

run-easy-strides.name: Easy run + strides
run-easy-strides.set: Easy, HR under LT1 · finish with 6 × 20″ strides, fully recovered (walk back)
run-easy-strides.why: Keeps mechanics and economy sharp. Short with full recovery, so it isn't a glycolytic stimulus that raises VLamax.

run-off-bike.name: Run off the bike
run-off-bike.set: Straight off the bike, easy, smooth cadence

run-long.name: Long run
run-long.set: Under LT1 HR the whole way, flat-ish route · gels from 60′
run-long.why: The run's ceiling builder: capillaries, mitochondria, durability.

run-hills-vo2.name: Hill VO2

steps.set: 20′ easy · 5 × 3′ uphill @ RPE 8–9, jog down · 15′ easy
20′ easy · 6 × 3′ uphill @ RPE 8–9, jog down · 15′ easy
20′ easy · 5 × 4′ uphill @ RPE 8–9, jog down · 15′ easy

run-hills-vo2.how: Run these on RPE. Deckard uses RPE for uphill VO2; HR lags and the heat adds about 10 bpm.
run-hills-vo2.why: VO2max stimulus with low impact and low injury risk.

run-vo2-k.name: 1 km VO2 reps

steps.set: 20′ easy · 5 × 1000 m @ VO2 pace (2′ jog) · 10′ easy
20′ easy · 6 × 1000 m @ VO2 pace (2′ jog) · 10′ easy

run-vo2-k.why: Keeps the ceiling while the block focuses on threshold and specificity.

run-threshold-mile.name: Threshold miles
run-threshold-mile.how: Deckard's track session. Finish at RPE 7–8; the last rep shouldn't be your fastest by much.
run-threshold-mile.why: Raises LT2 toward the ceiling. Threshold work also lowers VLamax.

run-tempo-8.name: Tempo → threshold 8′s

steps.set: 20′ easy · 4 × 8′ starting at MP, finishing at LT2 (2′ jog) · 10′ easy

run-tempo-8.why: Deckard's long-course threshold session. The MP→LT2 drift trains the range you race marathons in.

run-long-lt2.name: Long run with LT2 reps

steps.set: Easy 50′ · 4 × 5′ @ LT2 (2′ jog) · easy to finish
Easy 50′ · 5 × 5′ @ LT2 (2′ jog) · easy to finish
Easy 50′ · 6 × 5′ @ LT2 (2′ jog) · easy to finish

run-long-lt2.why: Threshold on tired legs: Deckard's 5 × 5′ inside a long run. Builds durability at LT2.

run-long-mp.name: Long run with MP

steps.set: Easy 40′ · 2 × 5 km @ MP (1 km easy) · easy to finish
Easy 35′ · 3 × 5 km @ MP (1 km easy) · easy to finish
Easy 30′ · 2 × 8 km @ MP (1 km easy) · easy to finish
Easy 25′ · 18 km @ MP · easy to finish

run-long-mp.how: Race-day fuelling: 60–90 g carbs/h, rehearse gels and drinks.
run-long-mp.why: Marathon specificity: hold MP while glycogen drops.

run-brick-rp.name: Race-pace brick run
run-brick-rp.set: Off the bike: 10′ easy · 15′ @ 70.3 run pace · 10′ easy
run-brick-rp.why: Finding race pace on legs that have just ridden.

run-test-mile.name: Run test: 1 mile TT
run-test-mile.set: 20′ easy + 4 strides · 1 mile (1609 m) ALL-OUT on track, even pace · 15′ easy
run-test-mile.why: Deckard's run anchor (≈ vVO2max). LT2 pace is read as % of it. A big gap means more threshold work; a small gap means keep building the ceiling.

run-race-ttt.name: TTT relay leg (~15 km beach)
run-race-ttt.set: Warm-up 15′ · your leg ~15 km on sand at LT2-ish effort · enjoy it
run-race-ttt.why: Side quest. Treat it as a hard threshold workout with friends, not an A race.

race-marathon.name: Marathon
race-marathon.set: 42.2 km. Even MP, fuel 60–90 g/h from km 5.

race-half.set: 1.9 km swim · 90 km bike @ 70.3 power · 21.1 km run

strength.name: Strength & mobility
strength.set: Heavy-ish: split squat, single-leg RDL, calf raise, step-up 3 × 6–8 · core 10′
strength.why: Running economy and injury resilience. Heavy, low reps, no fatigue chase.

swim-easy.name: Easy swim
swim-easy.set: Continuous easy with pull-buoy sets · technique focus (catch, rotation)
swim-easy.why: Fourth swim of the week: frequency builds feel and costs almost nothing.

weeks._comment: Templates sized to Lucas's demonstrated load (Jul–Sep 2026: 15.6 h/wk over 12 wk, ~15 sessions/wk with doubles). Minutes are for the first build week; later build weeks add ~7%.

base-volume._comment: Ceiling via volume: ~16 sessions, everything under LT1 except one bike 30/15 session. ~16 h in build week 1.

vo2-block._comment: Ceiling via intensity: bike 30/15s + run hills + swim VO2, volume held around ~15 h in build week 1.

durability._comment: The biggest easy volume of the year (~17.5 h → ~20 h): long run toward 2h20, long ride toward 3h50.

threshold-run._comment: Run-led threshold: 6 runs (≈70–80 km), with bike and swim kept honest (~14.5 h).

marathon-specific._comment: Marathon pace in the long run, MP→LT2 tempo, 1 km VO2 reps. 6 runs (~80 km) plus maintenance swim and bike (~14 h).

reset._comment: Unstructured: move every day, nothing hard, no plan to fail (~9 h at full size; reset weeks run at 50%).

bike-vo2-block._comment: Deckard's 7-week bike VO2max block: 30/15s + 4′ reps, swim VO2, run maintained (~16 h).

half-build._comment: 70.3 strength-endurance: torque, run tempo, race-pace bricks, 4 swims (~16 h).

half-specific._comment: Race rehearsal: threshold on the bike, long race-pace bricks, open water (~15.5 h).
